scope: Cancellable background STL encoding shared by GUI and public MCP
change: A disposable worker encodes STL without transferring workspace-owned input buffers. GUI exposes a cancel control, MCP cancellation uses job_cancel, and the project_export stage reports Encoding STL. Excluded point clouds and reference frames are filtered before accessing geometry.

focused.scope: Worker lifecycle and private Float64 topology, indexed normals, IO, automation API and MCP server before the additional progress-stage regression.
focused.subsequentChecks: The excluded-object and progress-stage regressions each failed before their fixes and passed afterward.

browser.mode: isolated Playwright Chrome; Browser plugin unavailable

review: Independent review identified excluded point-cloud materialization; a failing-then-passing regression and filter corrected it. A follow-up review found no further concrete defect.
priorAttempts: An initial browser driver failed after its checks because of a misplaced result-recording spread; its worker processes exited and temporary files were removed.
A second driver failed its console check because a quick Vite-only bundle lacked the offline service worker; the complete bundle retry passed.
limitations: Worker-start notification is emitted immediately before encoding; the test cancels after that notification and before a result, but does not pinpoint an instruction within the encoder.
Structured cloning of included ordinary geometry is synchronous and cannot itself be interrupted; shared immutable buffers are not transferred.
The large run is a single input; peak and timer-gap measurements do not establish general resource or responsiveness guarantees.
Missing or stale indexed topology still exports geometric facet normals; native equivalence for that case remains unverified.
Browser worker availability is required for interruptible encoding; the non-worker fallback remains synchronous.
The full M2 milestone still requires its remaining native, integration and exact-head hosted gates.
